item.title: Heineken document reveals worries over weight-loss drugs and beer sales
item.description: Heineken has urged British pubs and bars to adapt to the booming use of weight-loss drugs.
item.dc:creator: Emma Rumney
item.content:encoded: Heineken (HEIN.AS) has urged British pubs and bars to adapt to the booming use of weight-loss drugs or risk losing customers and revenue, according to a company presentation seen by Reuters, in a rare acknowledgement from a major alcohol maker that the medicines pose a threat to beer sales. The warning comes as GLP-1 use has surged, with some 10 million people taking medications like Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) Ozempic and Wegovy in the US last year, according to JPMorgan research. Their growth is having ramifications across the consumer goods industry, hitting [USN:L6N44E0VN TEXT:"cravings for sweets and snacks"], driving up [USN:L6N45R11L TEXT:"demand for clothing alterations"] and prompting a scramble to sell products that [USN:L6N4500ZA TEXT:"counter side-effects"]. Heineken, the world's second-largest brewer after AB InBev told hospitality customers that GLP-1 drugs can reduce the desire to drink and put pressure on beer and cider sales from "fullness and fewer serves", while warning that traditional multi-pint drinking occasions could become harder to sustain. The previously unreported presentation, sent to hospitality customers this month, advised venues to promote half-pints, low- and no-alcohol drinks and pair drinks with small plates, or risk declines in customer visits and spending as use of the medicines becomes increasingly mainstream in Britain. The alcohol industry is already grappling with years of falling sales in some major markets as consumers cut back on drinking for health and economic reasons. Heineken told Reuters the presentation was shared as part of its regular engagement with UK hospitality businesses to help them understand how the market is evolving. "We see some changes in consumption behaviour among (GLP-1) users and will continue to monitor how these behaviours evolve in 2027," Heineken said. GLP-1 users were not abandoning alcohol altogether but were increasingly opting for smaller serves, lower-alcohol drinks and more premium products, aligning with broader ongoing trends, it continued, adding its portfolio is well positioned to meet these demands. EVIDENCE OF REDUCED CONSUMPTION GROWS Europe is the Dutch brewer's largest market by revenue, but growth has been sluggish. Heineken has singled out Britain, where it owns more than 2,000 pubs, as a relative bright spot. Beer generated nearly £14 billion of sales in British pubs, bars and restaurants in the year to February 2026, with less than £300 million of that from no- and low-alcohol beers, according to a Heineken UK report. Although drinks companies have largely played down the threat from GLP-1 medicines, emerging spending data points to an impact on purchases. A group of US households with a GLP-1 user tracked by market research firm Circana between 2024 and 2026 reduced spending on alcohol for both at-home and out-of-home consumption compared with households without a user. After two years on the drugs, they spent about 7% less per month on alcohol versus non-using households, including around 13.5% less on beer. Top spirits maker Diageo (DGE.L) has told investors any impact from GLP-1 drugs should be manageable even if use becomes more widespread. Carlsberg (CARLb.CO) told Reuters existing data did not yet support the view that the drugs were a clear driver of beer consumption trends. Anheuser-Busch InBev (ABI.BR) declined to comment. Surveys in Europe and the UK by Circana, market researcher NIQ and specialist UK-based hospitality researcher KAM have also pointed to reduced drinking by GLP-1 users. Ten of 11 GLP-1 users Reuters interviewed said they had reduced their drinking, sometimes significantly, saying it left them feeling uncomfortable or unwell, or they simply no longer had any desire to drink. UK-based Daniel Cornwell, founder of hospitality executive recruitment business SPE Resourcing, said he used to drink regularly at work events and on weekends but now finds alcohol causes him discomfort and results in a multi-day hangover. GLP-1's effects on the brain may also affect users' motivation to drink, said Joseph Schacht, a professor at the University of Colorado Anschutz, who led a randomised controlled trial on the impact of GLP-1s on people with alcohol use disorder. He said trials have consistently shown a reduction in cravings and consumption for people with AUD. Schacht said the medicines could create a potential "Prozac moment" for AUD treatment, while also posing a challenge for alcohol producers if broader groups of drinkers cut back too. (This story has been corrected to add a dropped letter in the name in paragraph 16.)

item.title: Petróleo dispara US$3 com ataques houthis e vazamento; fecha no maior nível desde abril
item.description: Os preços do petróleo fecharam com alta de mais de US$3 nesta sexta-feira, atingindo o maior nível em quase seis meses, depois que ataques dos houthis na Arábia Saudita alimentaram preocupações com novas interrupções no abastecimento de energia proveniente do Oriente Médio, região onde as autoridades dos Emirados Árabes Unidos também relataram um derramamento de petróleo.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo fecharam com alta de mais de US$3 nesta sexta-feira, atingindo o maior nível em quase seis meses, depois que ataques dos houthis na Arábia Saudita alimentaram preocupações com novas interrupções no abastecimento de energia proveniente do Oriente Médio, região onde as autoridades dos Emirados Árabes Unidos também relataram um derramamento de petróleo. Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam a US$116,72 o barril, alta de US$3,55 ou 3,14%, atingindo o maior nível desde 29 de abril. O petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos Estados Unidos fechou a US$103,27 o barril, alta de US$3,80 ou 3,8%. O Brent encerrou a semana com alta de 6% e o WTI, com alta de 2,3%. “Os temores de interrupções no abastecimento impulsionaram a alta depois que rebeldes houthis, apoiados pelo Irã, realizaram uma série de ataques em toda a Arábia Saudita, inclusive contra infraestrutura energética”, disse Adam Turnquist, estrategista-chefe de ativos cruzados da LPL Financial. Na quinta-feira, a Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) ordenou a retirada de sua sede em Dhahran, no Golfo Pérsico, perto do Barein, informou a Reuters. Os combates se intensificaram entre a Arábia Saudita, maior exportadora mundial de petróleo, e os houthis, com base no Iêmen. Foi detectado um derramamento de petróleo proveniente de um petroleiro na costa de Umm Al Quwain, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, informou o Ministério das Mudanças Climáticas e do Meio Ambiente dos Emirados Árabes Unidos. O ministério não informou a causa do derramamento, e as autoridades ainda não identificaram o petroleiro envolvido. ATAQUES A EMBARCAÇÕES Fontes do setor de navegação informaram, em 9 de outubro, que o superpetroleiro Gem No. 2 foi atingido por um projétil não identificado a 13 milhas náuticas (24 km) a oeste de Al Jazeera, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos. “O mercado está preocupado com esses ataques iranianos contínuos a petroleiros, que temos visto aumentar na última semana”, disse Andrew Lipow, presidente da Lipow Oil Associates. “Embora tenha havido um aumento no transporte de petróleo pelo Estreito de Ormuz, isso pode mudar a qualquer momento.” Os confrontos entre os houthis e uma coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita, que apoia o governo internacionalmente reconhecido do Iêmen, se intensificaram desde que os houthis, alinhados com o Irã, avançaram em direção ao Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb no mês passado, um ponto de estrangulamento marítimo na foz do Mar Vermelho. Outubro foi o pior mês em termos de ataques à navegação comercial no Estreito de Ormuz e nas vias navegáveis próximas, de acordo com dados compilados por um think tank com sede em Washington que acompanha incidentes de segurança marítima em todo o mundo desde 2017. O presidente Donald Trump afirmou nesta sexta-feira que os Estados Unidos poderiam encerrar rapidamente a guerra com o Irã, mas acrescentou que talvez Washington devesse permitir que o conflito fosse se acalmando gradualmente.

item.title: Argentina drops probe into President Milei and sister over meme coin scandal
item.description: A criminal investigation into the role of Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister Karina Milei in a meme coin scandal was dropped on Friday, according to court records.
item.dc:creator: Leila Miller
item.content:encoded: A criminal investigation into the role of Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister Karina Milei in a meme coin scandal was dropped on Friday, according to court records. Federal judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi gave the order after prosecutor Eduardo Taiano asked for the dismissal, according to local outlet La Nacion. A judge was assigned in February 2025 to investigate Milei's role in promoting a cryptocurrency that crashed. Milei had recommended the little-known crypto coin $LIBRA in a posting on X, kicking off a brief rally. He later deleted the posting and denied having any link to the cryptocurrency, which soon plunged. The investigation had looked into possible fraud involved in the coin's launch. At the time of the currency's crash, Milei said he had acted "in good faith" and accused his political rivals of trying to take advantage of the situation.

item.title: CVS is trying out pharmacists in chronic health management
item.description: CVS Health Chief Medical Officer Dr. Amy Compton-Phillips on Friday said healthcare affordability and access could potentially improve if pharmacists in its 9,000 retail stores play a bigger role in chronic disease management, helping consumers stay on top of their most important health metrics.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Humer
item.content:encoded: CVS Health (CVS.N) Chief Medical Officer Dr. Amy Compton-Phillips on Friday said healthcare affordability and access could potentially improve if pharmacists in its 9,000 retail stores play a bigger role in chronic disease management, helping consumers stay on top of their most important health metrics. Each year, millions of Americans die from heart attacks, strokes, kidney disease, diabetes and other chronic conditions that can be treated with medical attention and proper medicines, she said. "We want to make it really easy and convenient for you to know your numbers," she said, adding that the company is experimenting with how pharmacists could become more involved by taking measurements for blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood sugar. CVS is starting now with a pilot in five stores in Michigan to try out the concept, she said. In the US, the role of pharmacists is determined in part by varying state pharmacy regulations. CVS Health is one of the largest US healthcare conglomerates, with the Aetna health insurance company, CVS Caremark pharmacy benefit manager and a nationwide network of retail pharmacies under its corporate umbrella. Compton-Phillips, speaking during the Reuters Total Health conference in Nashville, said the company was also talking to the government's Medicare agency about the role pharmacists could play in expanding access to healthcare and providing lower-cost healthcare. Affordability of healthcare is a key issue for the Trump administration, which is experimenting with different pilots that could lower costs for the more than 70 million people enrolled in the Medicare program for people aged 65 and older or with disabilities. One of the pilots involves more access to highly popular GLP-1 medications used to treat obesity, which the government has made available for $50 a month for a limited time [USN:S0N3WX02P TEXT:"through TrumpRx.gov"]. More companies, however, are [USN:L1N44L0V0 TEXT:"cutting corporate coverage"] of the medicines in 2027, recent surveys show, concerned about the increased cost to their health plans for the Eli Lilly (LLY.N) and Novo Nordisk (NOVOb.CO) medicines such as Mounjaro, Zepbound, Ozempic and Wegovy. Those medicines cost a few hundred dollars on the drugmakers' direct-pay websites, but can be more expensive to employers when they are covered in their insurance plans. Compton-Phillips said she would like to see better access to the GLP-1 drugs at a lower cost, describing their potential health benefits as "incredible." "They really do have real benefits in decreasing heart disease and kidney disease," she said. "I can't wait until 2032," she said. "That's when Ozempic goes generic in the US and I think we are going to be writing prescriptions for it like water."

item.title: Former MLB stars help kids swing for the fences in cricket-mad Mumbai
item.description: When former New York Yankees player Nick Swisher watched a schoolgirl with braided hair smash a series of home runs at a Mumbai playground, he was struck by how readily the cricket-mad youngsters could adapt their skills to baseball.
item.dc:creator: Revathi Hariharan
item.content:encoded: When former New York Yankees player Nick Swisher watched a schoolgirl with braided hair smash a series of home runs at a Mumbai playground, he was struck by how readily the cricket-mad youngsters could adapt their skills to baseball. The girl was among students at Hansraj Morarji School who swapped their cricket gear for baseball gloves as a parade of MLB greats arrived to put them through a series of drills. "I am taking these kids back with me, they can really swing the bat," the former Yankees first baseman and outfielder said. While Swisher ran home-run drills, former Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Adrian Gonzalez and American softball star Rachel Garcia oversaw batting practice. Meanwhile, former Chicago Cubs pitcher Jake Arrieta, ex-Boston Red Sox outfielder and World Series champion Jonny Gomes and softball star Jordan Woolery handled pitching and fielding sessions in Mumbai's scorching heat. Gonzalez, who hit 317 home runs in MLB across a 15-year career, said he was stunned by what he witnessed. "From how little baseball has been played in India, their skills are advanced," he said. "I kind of expected it because cricket has so many similarities to baseball: bat-to-ball skills, the ability to catch, especially catching with your hands. "I really feel like if India devoted time to baseball, you would have some Major League Baseball players in no time." The clinic showcased grassroots efforts to introduce baseball in a nation where cricket reigns supreme. GIRLS IMPRESS The former players also unanimously agreed that the girls consistently outperformed the boys, opening up the conversation about the future of women in baseball in India even as Indian women's cricket continues to shine. "I think the future for women in sports is growing. Hopefully in the next five to 10 years, we're going to be on top," Garcia said. "I'm excited to see what the future does look like and to keep inspiring young women to keep picking up a bat, ball or just going out there to try and play some sort of sport." Swisher, who has been watching cricket himself, said the sports complement each other. "The cricket swing does transfer to the baseball swing," he said. LOVE FOR THE GAME Ryo Takahashi, director of international business for MLB, remained optimistic about baseball's prospects in India despite the sport's limited presence, insisting that MLB was not competing with cricket. "I don't think it's fair to put a timeline on anybody for expectations, but I think if you saw what you saw today, the enthusiasm, the athleticism and most of all, just the love for the game, it could be very close," Takahashi said. "I think if kids play both, they'll be developing both skills in many ways." The former MLB players are scheduled to join Indian cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Deepak Chahar, Shardul Thakur and Radha Yadav for 3-on-3 baseball at the MLBx event on Saturday.

item.title: After previous day's slump, trading is quieter among AI shares
item.description: Big AI stocks were mixed on Friday, a day after the biggest decline in the Nasdaq Composite Index in four months, giving investors a welcome respite as they look forward to more information on Anthropic's forthcoming IPO and a further wave of earnings over the next week.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch
item.content:encoded: Big AI stocks were mixed on Friday, a day after the biggest decline in the Nasdaq Composite Index in four months, giving investors a welcome respite as they look forward to more information on Anthropic's forthcoming IPO and a further wave of earnings over the next week. Meta Platforms (META.O) , the center of Thursday's storm, was fractionally lower following [USN:L6N4690SJ TEXT:"Thursday's 7% decline"]. The operator of social media networks and major AI investor said in its earnings report this week that it would create a new class of shares in part to raise money for further capital spending, which was taken as evidence that the next leg of the AI buildout will be costly for shareholders. Other major AI players were mixed on Friday, with SpaceX (SPCX.O) , Oracle (ORCL.N) and Dell Technologies (DELL.N) up 1% to 2% and Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) down less than 1%. Big semiconductor stocks were mostly higher after their largest decline since the summer on Thursday. Credit default swaps tracking the perceived risk of default at the biggest AI players were mostly modestly lower, with Meta's five-year CDS spread trading 0.3% narrower at 123, according to LSEG data. The swaps enable investors to bet on a default using contracts typically with terms of five or 10 years, though contracts frequently change hands for the purposes of hedging positions and betting on near-term market moves. Thursday's deluge and the day-after calm is the latest sign of indirection in a market that has hovered near record highs without breaking out, said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey. "To some extent, we're seeing the market tread water over a longer period of time because every sell-off has been met by buyers and every point upward has been met by sellers," Meckler said. The Nasdaq (.IXIC) was barely changed on Friday afternoon. Credit-default swap premiums, reflecting the annual cost borne by the swap purchaser in thousands of dollars, have risen over the past year with concern about the risks being taken on by large AI spenders. The [USN:l4n4681e6 TEXT:"premiums rose"] on Thursday after Meta's decision to sell more stock, as much of the buildout to date has been financed through debt issuance. The concerns around AI spending and investment returns have added to the market's volatility since Treasury yields rose sharply in August, which changed the economics of investing and bond issuance, given the increasing attractiveness of a higher risk-free rate. It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B Riley Wealth in Boston. "There's no doubt at some point in time that the higher inflation moves, especially if driven by unsustainably higher energy prices ... would have to show up in corporate earnings. It hasn't yet, but that's the concern. And market participants are trying to position for that." Shares of neoclouds, smaller companies tied to AI data centers and other infrastructure projects like CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , have dropped due to anxiety over their future. Their performance of late has also raised talk on Wall Street that capital is growing scarce - which stands to raise costs further and potentially raise funding issues down the road. Even so, many investors remain positive on the sector, where giant AI lab Anthropic is expected to publish its IPO prospectus in coming days and Alphabet, Amazon (AMZN.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) are expected to report earnings next week. "In general, AI news in terms of revenues continues to be very strong, it's just at what cost and how long that growth is sustainable," Meckler said. "We really haven't gotten to the point of the market sort of focusing on winners and losers. It's been one big sector trade every day."

item.title: Leclerc marca el mejor tiempo para Ferrari en la primera sesión de pruebas del GP de EEUU
item.description: Charles Leclerc, de Ferrari, marcó el mejor tiempo en la primera sesión de pruebas del Gran Premio de Estados Unidos, celebrada el viernes en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin, mientras que el líder del campeonato, Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, apenas quedó quinto.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Charles Leclerc, de Ferrari, marcó el mejor tiempo en la primera sesión de pruebas del Gran Premio de Estados Unidos, celebrada el viernes en el Circuito de las Américas de Austin, mientras que el líder del campeonato, Kimi Antonelli, de Mercedes, apenas quedó quinto. El piloto nacido en Mónaco marcó la referencia con su monoplaza mejorado, con un tiempo de un minuto y 36,052 segundos, 0,084 más rápido que Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, que ha ganado las dos últimas carreras en Singapur y Malasia y que también se impuso en Austin el año pasado. Leclerc —cuyo monoplaza presenta modificaciones en el suelo, los pontones y el difusor— ganó en el circuito situado a las afueras de Austin en 2024. El vigente campeón de McLaren, Lando Norris, fue el tercero más rápido, a 0,245 del mejor tiempo, mientras que los Mercedes de George Russell y Antonelli fueron 0,326 y 0,481 más lentos que Leclerc, respectivamente. Antonelli, de 20 años, puede convertirse en el campeón de Fórmula 1 más joven de la historia si gana la carrera del domingo y los resultados le son favorables. De lo contrario, el italiano tendrá que esperar al menos hasta México, el fin de semana siguiente. Lewis Hamilton, de Ferrari, fue sexto en la tabla de tiempos, por delante de Oscar Piastri, de McLaren; Gabriel Bortoleto, de Audi; y la pareja de Racing Bulls formada por Arvid Lindblad y Liam Lawson. Tanto Lindblad como Bortoleto sufrirán penalizaciones en la parrilla de salida de la carrera del domingo tras cambiar componentes de la unidad de potencia. El circuito ha sido objeto de críticas por parte de algunos pilotos debido a lo accidentado que se ha vuelto. "Probablemente sea el circuito más bacheado que hemos tenido en lo que va de año. Es complicado, pero estoy seguro de que sabremos adaptarnos", declaró Pierre Gasly, de Alpine, a la cadena Sky Sports. Su compañero de equipo argentino, Franco Colapinto, sufrirá un retroceso de 10 puestos en la parrilla tras haber instalado una nueva unidad electrónica de control.

item.title: Infantino allana el camino para lograr su cuarto mandato en la FIFA
item.description: Las perspectivas de reelección del presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, se reforzaron después de que el máximo responsable del fútbol asiático respaldara su candidatura para un cuarto mandato, lo que dejó a Europa cada vez más aislada y puso de manifiesto la falta de un rival creíble.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Las perspectivas de reelección del presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, se reforzaron después de que el máximo responsable del fútbol asiático respaldara su candidatura para un cuarto mandato, lo que dejó a Europa cada vez más aislada y puso de manifiesto la falta de un rival creíble. El apoyo del presidente de la Confederación Asiática de Fútbol, el jeque Salman bin Ibrahim Al Jalifa, expresado el viernes en el congreso extraordinario de la AFC celebrado en Tokio, supuso una notable reconciliación con Infantino. El jeque Salman se había sumado al presidente de la UEFA, Aleksander Ceferin, y al presidente de la CONCACAF, Víctor Montagliani, en las críticas a la propuesta "FIFA Forward Enterprise" (FFE), que buscaba inversión privada para una nueva entidad que controlara los derechos comerciales vinculados a las principales competiciones de la FIFA, incluida la Copa Mundial. Su oposición pública, seguida de llamamientos a la dimisión de Infantino, suscitó dudas sobre si la hasta entonces sólida base de apoyo del presidente de la FIFA estaba empezando a resquebrajarse. Sin embargo, el jeque Salman dijo ante el congreso de la AFC que Asia se mantenía unida en apoyo a Infantino, dos meses después de que la confederación le acusara de una "violación fundamental de la confianza" en relación con la iniciativa FFE. El giro redujo las posibilidades de cualquier rival de cara a las elecciones de marzo. Asia cuenta con 47 federaciones, aunque solo 46 son miembros de la FIFA con derecho a voto en las elecciones presidenciales. Cada federación nacional dispone de un voto en las elecciones de la FIFA, independientemente del tamaño del país o de su trayectoria futbolística. Infantino ya se había asegurado el apoyo de la confederación africana, compuesta por 54 miembros, con la que ha mantenido sólidas relaciones durante su presidencia. La CONMEBOL de Sudamérica solo cuenta con 10 votos, pero no se sumó a las peticiones de dimisión, y se espera que la mayoría de las federaciones de Oceanía también se mantengan de su lado. La CONCACAF se había sumado inicialmente a la UEFA y a la AFC en las críticas a Infantino, pero sus federaciones miembro están ahora divididas, y miembros influyentes, como México, respaldan al actual presidente. El respaldo de las confederaciones no es formalmente vinculante para las asociaciones individuales, pero el apoyo con el que cuenta Infantino en Asia, África y otras regiones le otorga una posición dominante entre los 211 miembros con derecho a voto de la FIFA antes de que se cierre el plazo de presentación de candidaturas el 18 de noviembre.

item.title: Lawyers gird for congressional probes if Democrats take control
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
item.dc:creator: David Thomas, Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com ) A Democratic takeover of at least one chamber of Congress following next month's midterm elections could be a boon to law firms angling for roles in a potential surge of congressional investigations. Several lawyers and lobbyists in Washington said they're communicating with current and potential clients in anticipation of a spate of new probes on Capitol Hill if Democrats tip the balance. Reuters [USN:L1N4600WS TEXT:"has reported"] that Democrats are widely expected to win control of the House, though the Senate is too close to call. Anyone ignoring inquiries from Democratic lawmakers risks the chance they could have subpoena power in the next Congress, said Brian Pomper, who co-leads Akin Gump's lobbying and public policy practice. "They should really be preparing now," Pomper said. After two years in the minority during Republican President Donald Trump's first term, newly-empowered Democrats could scrutinize [USN:L6N45E0PR TEXT:"a range of targets"], from administration figures to corporate donors and participants in business deals brokered by the Trump family. Unlike the White House, private companies cannot claim that their activities are protected by executive privilege. Democrats are "telegraphing that they’re going to go towards companies for information" because the administration will not cooperate, said Susanne Sachsman Grooms, the leader of Cooley's congressional investigations practice. Grooms said she is planning to meet with a small group of clients at private dinners in New York and San Francisco after the election to discuss the results and their implications. US law firm Brownstein Hyatt launched a website to track investigative activity, said Will Moschella, who co-chairs the firm's government relations department, and posted hundreds of letters Democratic lawmakers in the US House and Senate have sent since last year that could augur future probes. Lawyers at several firms said they expanded their congressional investigations practices over the past year, while others are still hiring. In March, Akin Gump [USN:L6N40C15X TEXT:"hired Marcus Childress"], a former senior adviser to US Representative Jamie Raskin, the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee and a Democrat. Last month, Cooley brought Jessica Donlon, who has served as general counsel to Republican US Representatives Brett Guthrie and James Comer. Aaron Cutler, who leads Hogan Lovells Cadwalader's government relations practice, said he has been given a mandate to hire more people. "We've been busy all year," Cutler said. "We're expecting to be busier next year." LOBBYING REVENUES ON THE RISE – AGAIN Several firms reported record-setting US lobbying revenues once again in the third quarter, as lobbyists also look ahead to the post-election landscape. Florida-founded lobbying firm Ballard Partners said it brought in $35.01 million in its best-ever quarter, 39.6% more than the same time period last year. The firm, which previously employed former US Attorney General Pam Bondi, has seen massive revenue growth since President Donald Trump took office last year. Law firms Brownstein Hyatt, Akin Gump and Squire Patton Boggs reported federal lobbying revenues of $22.5 million, $18.85 million and $7.9 million, respectively, while lobbying firms BGR Group and Cornerstone Government Affairs reported $22.5 million and $15.6 million. Representatives from those five firms said these are new quarterly records. Akin Gump said lobbying on trade and tariff issues was a major driver, while Brownstein Hyatt cited a range of areas including healthcare and tax. Lobbyists are required to report quarterly revenue under the federal Lobbying Disclosure Act. Not every firm saw an increase. Hogan Lovells Cadwalader said its federal lobbying revenue in the third quarter dropped to $2.97 million from $3.7 million in the prior quarter. K&L Gates reported a quarterly decline from $5.5 million to $4.8 million. Aaron Cutler, the leader of Hogan Lovells Cadwalader's government relations practice, said in a statement the firm has "continued to see an increase in non-LDA work," including congressional investigations and its work for foreign clients like Venezuela. Karishma Shah Page, who co-leads K&L Gates' public policy and law practice, said in an email that there was heavy preparation underway ahead of the election, and that she expects both the end of the year and the next congressional session to be busy. She noted that the third quarter tends to be slower prior to a midterm election, and that Congress spent limited time in session in July and September. Federal lobbying spending has continually increased since 2016, surpassing $5 billion last year, according to nonprofit research group OpenSecrets. As of July 23, companies, trade groups and other entities have spent $2.74 billion this year, per OpenSecrets. COOLEY MATCHES MILBANK SALARY SCALE Cooley will raise salaries for its US associates in January, aligning with the associate compensation scale that rival firm Milbank rolled out earlier this year. Associates at Palo Alto-founded Cooley will have base salaries ranging from $235,000 to $455,000, depending on seniority, according to an internal Cooley memo published by the website Above the Law. The firm will also hand out “special” bonuses for the year to eligible associates, the memo said, without specifying the amounts. Large US firms have largely stayed quiet since Milbank announced [USN:L6N42A13E TEXT:"salary increases"] in June, though McDermott, Will & Schulte was among a handful of firms that matched the new scale. Milbank, which in recent years has been a first mover among large firms on associate compensation, also rolled out so-called [USN:L6N43T126 TEXT:"special bonuses"] of up to $25,000 in July.
