item.title: Zelenski dice negociadores ucranianos, rusos y estadounidenses se reunirán en Abu Dabi
item.description: El presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, declaró el viernes que los negociadores de paz de Ucrania, Rusia y Estados Unidos habían acordado reunirse a nivel técnico durante la primera quincena de noviembre en Abu Dabi, y añadió que esperaba que a ello le siguiera una reunión entre los líderes de estos países.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: El presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, declaró el viernes que los negociadores de paz de Ucrania, Rusia y Estados Unidos habían acordado reunirse a nivel técnico durante la primera quincena de noviembre en Abu Dabi, y añadió que esperaba que a ello le siguiera una reunión entre los líderes de estos países. Zelenski afirmó que había hablado el viernes con los enviados estadounidenses Jared Kushner y Steve Witkoff tras la reunión que estos mantuvieron con el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, a principios de esta semana. Señaló que cualquier acuerdo de paz necesitaría sólidas garantías de seguridad para Ucrania y financiación durante diez años para mantener el ejército ucraniano. "El plan es reunirnos en la primera quincena de noviembre y, por supuesto, lo antes posible", declaró Zelenski al centro de estudios Hudson Institute a través de una videoconferencia. Señaló que mucho dependería de Rusia, y destacó que una reunión similar prevista para este mes no se había materializado. Zelenski subrayó la importancia de proseguir con los esfuerzos diplomáticos para alcanzar un alto el fuego y poner fin a la guerra, que ya cumple su quinto año, y añadió que Europa también debería participar en las negociaciones. El presidente ucraniano señaló que era fundamental que las conversaciones técnicas fueran seguidas de una reunión entre los líderes de estos países. Manifestó su esperanza de celebrar otra reunión con los negociadores estadounidenses y añadió que Ucrania estaba dispuesta a iniciar negociaciones sobre un alto el fuego total, o incluso un acuerdo que abarcara únicamente el sector energético o las operaciones marítimas, si Moscú no estuviera dispuesta a debatir un acuerdo más amplio. La Casa Blanca no hizo ningún comentario inmediato sobre los planes de celebrar una reunión trilateral a nivel técnico.

item.title: Novartis presenta datos sobre fármaco para esclerosis múltiple peores de lo esperado
item.description: El fármaco oral remibrutinib para la esclerosis múltiple (EM) de la farmacéutica suiza Novartis redujo significativamente las recaídas en los pacientes, según los datos presentados el viernes en un congreso médico celebrado en Toronto, pero menos de lo que esperaban los analistas.
item.dc:creator: Bhanvi Satija, Marleen Kaesebier
item.content:encoded: El fármaco oral remibrutinib para la esclerosis múltiple (EM) de la farmacéutica suiza Novartis (NOVN.S) redujo significativamente las recaídas en los pacientes, según los datos presentados el viernes en un congreso médico celebrado en Toronto, pero menos de lo que esperaban los analistas. El fármaco redujo las tasas de recaída anualizadas en un 35,2% y un 31,2%, en comparación con la teriflunomida, un tratamiento más antiguo para la EM comercializado por Sanofi bajo la marca Aubagio. Los analistas esperaban una reducción de entre el 45% y el 60%. Los resultados detallados del ensayo, que anteriormente solo se habían dado a conocer de forma resumida, se presentaron [USN:L6N4670V1 TEXT:"días después de que Roche"] (ROPC.S) publicara sus propios datos sobre el fármaco rival para la EM, el fenebrutinib. En los datos agrupados de la fase III, Roche informó de una reducción del 55% en la tasa de recaídas anualizada frente a la teriflunomida. "En definitiva, podrían ser bastante similares en lo que hacen en cuanto a la reducción de las recaídas y la discapacidad", dijo Heinz Wiendl, copresidente de los estudios de Novartis, en una entrevista. Antes de la publicación de los resultados, los analistas señalaron que se necesitarían mejoras en las recidivas similares a las observadas en el ensayo de Roche para demostrar que esta clase de tratamientos es mejor que las terapias anti-CD20 que se utilizan actualmente. Entre estas se incluyen Ocrevus, Kesimpta de Novartis y Briumvi de TG Therapeutics (TGTX.O) , que se dirigen a las células inmunitarias que provocan la EM y las destruyen. Novartis confía en el éxito del fármaco en diferentes áreas terapéuticas, especialmente tras una serie de reveses recientes en los ensayos de su fármaco para el corazón, pelacarsen, y de su tratamiento para la debilidad muscular, del-desiran. Los analistas estiman actualmente que el remibrutinib podría alcanzar unas ventas máximas de más de 4.000 millones de dólares, si se aprueba para pacientes con formas recidivantes de EM. Los dos fármacos competidores para la EM pertenecen a una clase de tratamientos que anteriormente se relacionaban con toxicidad hepática, lo que hace que la seguridad sea un aspecto que se sigue muy de cerca. Aunque el fenebrutinib de Roche podría tener una ventaja en términos de eficacia, mostró elevaciones significativamente mayores de las enzimas hepáticas en comparación con el fármaco de referencia. Novartis dijo que no se observaron señales de seguridad hepática en su fármaco.

item.title: Plantio de soja em Mato Grosso segue adiantado, com 75,81% das áreas semeadas, diz Imea
item.description: O plantio de soja em Mato Grosso, principal produtor brasileiro, atingiu 75,81% da área projetada para o Estado até esta sexta-feira, um salto de 23,95 pontos percentuais em relação à semana anterior, de acordo com dados publicados pelo Instituto Mato-grossense de Economia Agropecuária (Imea).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O plantio de soja em Mato Grosso, principal produtor brasileiro, atingiu 75,81% da área projetada para o Estado até esta sexta-feira, um salto de 23,95 pontos percentuais em relação à semana anterior, de acordo com dados publicados pelo Instituto Mato-grossense de Economia Agropecuária (Imea). O índice indica um ritmo mais acelerado em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado (60,05%) e na comparação com a média de cinco anos para a época (64,31%), segundo dados do instituto ligado aos produtores. O plantio se acelerou em outubro, com uma melhora nas chuvas, após um ritmo considerado abaixo do ideal em setembro. Se o ritmo atual for mantido, o Mato Grosso deverá superar 80% da área semeada na última semana de outubro, o que amplia a perspectiva de que a maior parte da área de milho de segunda safra seja implantada dentro da janela ideal, segundo avaliação do Imea divulgada em nota da Federação da Agricultura e Pecuária de Mato Grosso. Quase todo o milho semeado em Mato Grosso vem da segunda safra, após a colheita da soja. Se o cereal é implantado dentro da melhor janela climática, os riscos diminuem.

item.title: Canadian dollar hits five-week high as data supports rate hike bets
item.description: The Canadian dollar strengthened to a five-week high against its US counterpart on Friday as oil prices rose and domestic retail sales data supported expectations the Bank of Canada would raise interest rates next week.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar strengthened to a five-week high against its US counterpart on Friday as oil prices rose and domestic retail sales data supported expectations the Bank of Canada would raise interest rates next week. The loonie was trading 0.1% higher at 1.40 per US dollar, or 71.43 US cents, after touching its strongest intraday level since September 16 at 1.3969. It left the currency on track for a seventh straight day of gains, which would be the longest daily winning streak since March 2022. For the week, the currency was up 1% — heading for its biggest weekly advance since April. [USN:L6N4690T5 TEXT:"Canadian retail sales"] rose 1.2% in August from July, led by higher sales at motor vehicle and parts dealers, while a preliminary estimate showed sales increasing by 0.7% in September. "Given the resilience in these spending numbers, we still believe the Bank of Canada is headed for a rate increase next week," Oskar Stone, an analyst at Desjardins, said in a note, adding that the data points to third-quarter GDP growth of 2%. The Bank of Canada will raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists [USN:L6N4690GZ TEXT:"polled by Reuters"]. Investors see a roughly 80% chance the BoC hikes next week. Bets on a hike have increased in recent days after hawkish comments from [USN:L6N463037 TEXT:"Governor Tiff Macklem"] and as [USN:L6N4651AT TEXT:"Alberta"] voted by a large majority to remain part of Canada. The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, rose after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East. US crude oil futures settled 3.8% higher at $103.27 a barrel. Canadian bond yields rose across the curve, tracking moves in US Treasuries. The 10-year was up 5.1 basis points at 3.838%.

item.title: Indycar returns to Europe after 20 year absence with home race for Palou
item.description: US-based Indycar will race in Europe for the first time in 20 years with a July 2027 round at Barcelona's Circuit de Catalunya in a multi-year deal announced on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US-based Indycar will race in Europe for the first time in 20 years with a July 2027 round at Barcelona's Circuit de Catalunya in a multi-year deal announced on Friday. The race will be a return home for Spain's five-time Indycar champion Alex Palou, who was born near Barcelona. Indycar last raced in Europe at the Assen circuit in the Netherlands in 2007. The championship has not raced outside North America since 2013, when there was a race in Brazil. Palou, 29, has won the last four Indycar titles and also won the Indianapolis 500 in 2025. The Circuit de Catalunya hosted Formula One this year but drops off the calendar in 2027 and will [USN:L6N3ZC0JK TEXT:"alternate with Belgium until 2032. "] "We’ve been witnessing his (Palou's) extraordinary talent for years, and we know that his fans in Spain have been eager to see him compete live," said Mark Miles, CEO of Indycar owner Penske Entertainment Corp. "It is an amazing opportunity, and it means so much to me to have a race at home in Barcelona, it’s hard to put into words. I know the fans are going to love it, and I think we are going to put on a great show," said Palou. The 2027 race will be held on July 16-18.

item.title: Leclerc laps fastest for Ferrari in first US GP practice
item.description: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc lapped fastest in first practice for the US Grand Prix at Austin's Circuit of the Americas on Friday with Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli only fifth.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc lapped fastest in first practice for the US Grand Prix at Austin's Circuit of the Americas on Friday with Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli only fifth. The Monaco-born driver set the standard in his upgraded car with a time of one minute 36.052 seconds, 0.084 faster than Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who has won the previous two races in Singapore and Malaysia and was also triumphant in Austin last year. Leclerc -- whose car has changes to the floor, sidepod and diffuser -- won at the circuit outside Austin in 2024. McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris was third fastest, 0.245 off the pace, with the Mercedes of George Russell and Antonelli 0.326 and 0.481 slower than Leclerc respectively. Antonelli, 20, can become the youngest ever Formula One champion if he wins Sunday's race and results go his way. Otherwise the Italian will have to wait until at least Mexico the weekend after. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was sixth on the timesheets ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto and Racing Bulls pair Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson. Lindblad and Bortoleto are both set to take grid penalties for Sunday's race after power unit component changes. The track has drawn [USN:L6N469119 TEXT:"criticism from some drivers"] for how bumpy it has become. "Probably the bumpiest track we've had so far this year. It's tricky but I'm sure we'll work around it," Alpine's Pierre Gasly told Sky Sports television. His Argentine teammate Franco Colapinto will have a 10-place grid drop after a new control electronics unit was fitted.

item.title: US Justice Dept sues to block possible Alaska election of Democrat to Senate
item.description: Control of the US Senate could come down to Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan is running a closely contested race against Democrat Mary Peltola.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department on Thursday sued to preemptively block Alaska from certifying the results of its US Senate race if the Republican incumbent candidate loses by a narrow margin, saying voters could be confused because two Republicans on the ballot have almost identical names. The lawsuit signals the willingness of President Donald Trump's administration to contest the results of the November 3 midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress. Trump's administration has taken an increasingly aggressive approach to election oversight, pressing states for voter-registration data and arguing that stricter measures are needed to ensure public confidence in the vote. Critics, including both Democratic and some Republican election officials, view the moves as federal overreach. Control of the US Senate could come down to Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan is running a closely contested race against Democrat Mary Peltola. The Justice Department's lawsuit , filed in federal court in Anchorage, takes issue with the presence of a third contender in the race, another Republican named Dan J. Sullivan Jr, alleging he is running "with the intention of misleading supporters of Senator Sullivan into voting for him." The lawsuit asks a federal judge to block the certification of an outcome "that may be impacted by voter confusion," so that there can be "an investigation to determine whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan." Trump told reporters on Friday that he supported the lawsuit, saying "I'm the one that said do it." A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement that the agency is taking "necessary steps to ensure that this frivolous candidacy does not undermine the integrity of Alaska’s election or the will of its voters.” Election officials around the country have told Reuters they are preparing for potential federal interference in November’s elections, including legal challenges and disputes over voting that could disrupt certification of the results. Trump has a long history of challenging election outcomes and encouraging supporters to contest results he views as unfavorable. Election law experts said the Justice Department's lawsuit has no merit and seeks relief not allowed under federal law. "In short, like many Department letters over the last few years, it is designed to win the press release rather than the litigation," wrote Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller in a blog post , adding that "the legal argument is one of the worst ones I’ve ever seen." Trump's administration "has absolutely no authority to tell Alaska when or how to certify the results of its Senate election," said David Becker of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, a nonpartisan group that advises election officials, adding that "this issue has already been fully litigated by Alaska's courts." The unelected Sullivan, a former US Forest Service worker and elementary school teacher, filed to run as a candidate on May 29 seeking to unseat Senator Dan S. Sullivan and "put Alaska first," according to his campaign website, which advertised "Dan Sullivan Challenges Dan Sullivan for US Senate Seat." Dan J. Sullivan has denied in interviews with US news outlets that his aim is to cause confusion or divert votes from Dan S. Sullivan. The Alaska Supreme Court in June permitted the unelected Sullivan to appear on the ballot. He will appear without a party designation next to his name, while the senator will be listed as the Republican incumbent. Trump's [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"approval rating"] has fallen to a record low, hit by rising diesel and gasoline prices and a conflict in the Middle East that has proven deeply unpopular with voters. Public opinion polls suggest Republicans may lose control of one or both houses of Congress, which would likely limit Trump's ability to enact his policies in the final two years of his presidency.

item.title: Advantage Infantino as AFC backing puts FIFA president on track for fourth term
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino's reelection prospects have strengthened significantly after the head of Asian football endorsed his bid for a fourth term, leaving Europe increasingly isolated and exposing the lack of a credible challenger.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: FIFA President Gianni Infantino's reelection prospects have strengthened significantly after the head of Asian football endorsed his bid for a fourth term, leaving Europe increasingly isolated and exposing the lack of a credible challenger. Asian Football Confederation President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa's endorsement, delivered at the [USN:L1N46902J TEXT:"AFC extraordinary congress in Tokyo"] on Friday, marked a striking reconciliation with Infantino. Sheikh Salman had joined UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and CONCACAF chief Victor Montagliani in criticising the [USN:L6N43Y023 TEXT:"FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal"], which sought private investment in a new entity controlling commercial rights linked to major FIFA competitions, including the World Cup. Their public opposition, followed by calls for Infantino to resign, raised questions about whether the FIFA president's previously solid support base was beginning to fracture. But Sheikh Salman told the AFC's congress that Asia was united behind Infantino, two months after the confederation accused him of a [USN:L6N4470F3 TEXT:""fundamental breach of trust""] over the venture. The turnaround has significantly narrowed the path for any challenger ahead of the March election. ELECTORAL ARITHMETIC Asia has 47 member associations, although only 46 are FIFA members eligible to vote in the presidential election. Each national federation has one vote in the FIFA election regardless of the country's size or its football pedigree. Infantino had already [USN:L6N4431BC TEXT:"secured support from Africa's 54-member confederation"], where he has enjoyed strong relationships throughout his presidency. South America's CONMEBOL has only 10 votes but did not join calls for his resignation, while most of Oceania's associations are also expected to remain in his camp. CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America and the Caribbean, had initially joined UEFA and the AFC in criticising Infantino, but its member associations are now divided, with influential members including Mexico backing the incumbent. Confederation endorsements do not formally bind individual associations, but the support available to Infantino across Asia, Africa and elsewhere gives him a commanding position among FIFA’s 211 voting members before nominations close on November 18. That leaves UEFA, with its 55 associations, as the main centre of opposition, but even unanimous European support for another candidate would account for little more than a quarter of the electorate. UEFA ISOLATED UEFA has remained critical of Infantino and [USN:L1N4660LK TEXT:"continues to seek answers"] regarding the abandoned FFE project and broader governance issues. Europe, however, has not yet produced a [USN:L6N4580Z7 TEXT:"credible challenger"] and is increasingly isolated in its opposition to Infantino, whose strength has always rested on building alliances beyond football's traditional power centres. Sheikh Salman, Ceferin and Montagliani questioned both the substance of the FFE proposal and the way it had been presented. Infantino subsequently abandoned the project and [USN:L8N4611Y3 TEXT:"apologised over the way it had been handled"] at a closed FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last week. The apology failed to sway European football associations but Sheikh Salman said in Tokyo that the two men had reached an understanding and should now "move forward". Infantino's swift retreat and the promise of allocating $25 million to each association appear to have helped repair damaged relationships. "In ten years since I became FIFA President, we have gone from $1 million per FIFA Member Association to $25 million each – all across the world," Infantino said. "I would like to thank everyone who has made suggestions over the past few months on the distribution of FIFA's funds to our 211 FIFA Member Associations as we need to look forward in a spirit of unity and in the best interests of football." Sheikh Salman's endorsement suggests the crisis that threatened to complicate Infantino's reelection campaign has so far cost him little lasting political support. Unless UEFA can quickly produce a challenger capable of building support beyond Europe, the election increasingly looks less like a contest over Infantino's leadership than a demonstration of his continuing command of the electorate.

item.title: Roger Goodell: NFL targeting Tokyo for game in 2027 or 2028
item.description: The NFL expects to be playing a regular-season game in Tokyo in either 2027 or 2028, commissioner Roger Goodell said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NFL expects to be playing a regular-season game in Tokyo in either 2027 or 2028, commissioner Roger Goodell said on Friday. "Listen, Tokyo is clearly on our list, whether it's next year or the year after. It's coming at some point in the near future," Goodell told NFL Daily. "We're going to continue to focus on our priority markets, which a lot of them they've been in, but there are other cities; this year, we went to Rio (de Janeiro) rather than Sao Paulo. Goodell was quick to point to the power of the NFL with its trip to Melbourne, Australia, for a Week 1 encounter between the San Francisco 49ers and rival Los Angeles Rams. "On a Friday morning at 10:30 (a.m. local time), to have 100,000 people in the stadium, it was just an incredible feeling for us. I think it's opened up new opportunities for us," Goodell said. "The travel is something we think we can manage and do it without impacting negatively on the teams. So, each of these we learned something from and we benefit and we also open those other doors. "We're planning on playing global. That's where we're going." The NFL has played five of its nine international games thus far this season. Goodell was in Paris on Friday in advance of the Pittsburgh Steelers' game on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. The league's second trip to Spain takes place in Week 9 with the Cincinnati Bengals battling the Atlanta Falcons on Nov. 8 in Madrid. Next up is Germany, where the New England Patriots will meet the Detroit Lions in Week 10 on Nov. 15 in Munich. The final international offering features the Minnesota Vikings and 49ers in Mexico City in Week 11 on Nov. 22 The NFL previously played 14 exhibition games in Japan, with the last one pitting the Falcons against the Indianapolis Colts in 2005. --Field Level Media

item.title: POLL Bank of Canada to raise rates to 2.50% on October 28 and once again by end-March
item.description: The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Nushaiba Iqbal
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters. Inflation rose to [USN:L6N4620VU TEXT:"3.1%"] in September, only barely overshooting the BoC's target range of 1% to 3%. But the central bank's latest [USN:BCLJLEM2I TEXT:"business outlook survey"] showed sharply rising inflation expectations in the run-up to a recent breakdown in trade talks with the United States, Canada's main export destination. Quarterly inflation forecasts from the bank, also due next week, are likely to be [USN:L6N463037 TEXT:"revised higher"], BoC Governor Tiff Macklem told reporters in remarks Saturday that markets interpreted as a hint a rate rise is coming. Interest rate futures have moved from pricing in a 30% chance of a rate hike in October to around a three-in-four likelihood. Many economists this week changed their view from a hold to a hike, citing those remarks from Macklem. "What changed the tone in the governor's public comments on the weekend and what changed our view on Monday is the same source, and that is the responses from the BoC's business outlook and consumer surveys," said Royce Mendes, managing director and head of macro strategy at Desjardins. "So presumably the governor had seen the results before they were published more broadly on Monday. And I would assume that informed his public commentary," Mendes said. "The survey responses...suggest there are more serious inflationary pressures coming." Nineteen of 34 economists surveyed in the October 21-23 poll, or 56% of them, said the BoC will hike its overnight rate by a quarter percentage point to 2.50%, its first move in a year. This is a clear reversal from the previous poll, when 80% of respondents forecast the bank would hold its rate at 2.25% until the end of 2026, and two-thirds of them forecast a hold until the end of March 2027. Those economists who forecast no move next week mainly cited a weak economy and subdued inflation pressures despite soaring oil prices , which hit $117 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday. Sixteen of 29 respondents, a 55% majority, also forecast one more rise before March 2027, after which policymakers would hold the overnight rate at 2.75%, poll medians showed. If correct, it will be the shortest BoC policy tightening campaign in 30 years. But even a short series of hikes would bring the BoC into a widening group of central banks that have opted for tighter monetary policy in response to persistent inflation emerging as a result of the US-led [USN:L6N46718Z TEXT:"war"] with Iran that began in February. Among major central banks, only the BoC and the Bank of England — which is [USN:L6N4610Q9 TEXT:"widely expected"] to raise rates at its early November meeting — have not yet begun to raise rates. But many say the BoC will need to be measured with the pace of rate increases given other risks to the economy. Benjamin Reitzes, Canadian rates and macro strategist at BMO, said: "They'd rather make the mistake of hiking a little bit too early, which means maybe they have to hike a little bit less at the end of the day than falling behind the curve, which is what happened in 2021-2022, and they don't want to repeat that mistake.” Economic growth likely slowed to 1.9% last quarter from 3.3% [USN:L6N44O17F TEXT:"in Q2"] and is forecast at 1.3% in the current one before accelerating next year, poll medians showed. The economy will grow 1.0% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, the survey found. Inflation will average 2.8% for 2026 as a whole, falling to 2.3% in 2027, poll medians showed. ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

item.title: Macron dice tiroteo terrorista en barrio de las afueras de París marca punto de inflexión para Francia
item.description: El presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, calificó el tiroteo del viernes en Trappes, cerca de París, como un atentado terrorista y racista que ha marcado un punto de inflexión en la historia de Francia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, calificó el tiroteo del viernes en Trappes, cerca de París, como un atentado terrorista y racista que ha marcado un punto de inflexión en la historia de Francia. Macron afirmó que las víctimas del tirador de Trappes fueron elegidas como objetivo únicamente por su religión y el color de su piel. "Lo ocurrido hoy marca un punto de inflexión para la República y para nuestro país. Lo ocurrido hoy ha sido un atentado terrorista y racista", declaró Macron a los periodistas el viernes.

item.title: Zelenskiy diz que negociadores ucranianos, russos e norte-americanos se reunirão no início de novembro em Abu Dhabi
item.description: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse nesta sexta-feira que os negociadores de paz da Ucrânia, da Rússia e dos Estados Unidos concordaram em se reunir em nível técnico na primeira quinzena de novembro, em Abu Dhabi, acrescentando que espera que isso seja seguido por um encontro entre os líderes desses países.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: O presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, disse nesta sexta-feira que os negociadores de paz da Ucrânia, da Rússia e dos Estados Unidos concordaram em se reunir em nível técnico na primeira quinzena de novembro, em Abu Dhabi, acrescentando que espera que isso seja seguido por um encontro entre os líderes desses países. Zelenskiy disse ter conversado com os enviados dos EUA, Jared Kushner e Steve Witkoff, nesta sexta-feira, após a reunião deles com o presidente da Rússia, Vladimir Putin, no início desta semana. Ele afirmou que qualquer acordo de paz precisará de fortes garantias de segurança para a Ucrânia e de financiamento por 10 anos para manter o Exército ucraniano. “O plano é nos reunirmos na primeira quinzena de novembro e, o mais cedo possível, é claro”, disse Zelenskiy ao think tank Hudson Institute por meio de uma videoconferência. Ele afirmou que muito dependeria da Rússia, observando que uma reunião semelhante prevista para este mês não havia se concretizado. Zelenskiy enfatizou a importância de esforços diplomáticos contínuos para alcançar um cessar-fogo e pôr fim à guerra, que já está em seu quinto ano, acrescentando que a Europa também deveria participar das negociações. O presidente ucraniano disse que é fundamental que as discussões técnicas sejam seguidas por uma reunião dos líderes dos países. (Reportagem de Andrea Shalal)

item.title: Mark Cuban says AI hack agents are like cockroaches, but can be controlled
item.description: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said on Friday that he is "not a doomer" about artificial intelligence and that companies should be able to use the technology to protect themselves from AI-driven hacks by agents that he compared to cockroaches.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Humer
item.content:encoded: Billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said on Friday that he is "not a doomer" about artificial intelligence and that companies should be able to use the technology to protect themselves from AI-driven hacks by agents that he compared to cockroaches. "It's like the cockroach thing, right? You build a new house, you get the guys to come out and spray... the one thing I don't want is cockroaches in my house ever. But the cockroaches find a way to get in because there's zillions of them, right? And then if there's one gets in, there's more that are going to get in, and that's kind of the way AI works," Cuban said, speaking at Reuters Total Health. "It's all brute force acts, and if it's brute force on that side with the bad guys, you can also use brute force with the good guys," he said. Cuban, famous for his role on business reality show "Shark Tank" and his involvement in the Dallas Mavericks NBA team, ventured into healthcare when he started the online pharmacy Cost Plus Drug Company in 2022 with a standard pricing scheme: the cost it pays for the drug, plus 15%. In May, Cost Plus signed on with TrumpRx.gov, a website created by the Trump administration selling discounted weight-loss drugs. But the company has also moved into manufacturing. In 2025, it began making sterile injectable drugs typically used in hospitals in its own compounding manufacturing facility. Cuban said the company has built smaller, tractor-trailer-sized manufacturing facilities he calls "pods" that can be used separately or together to manufacture many kinds of drugs, including generics and treatments for rare diseases. He said the pods would eventually be Cost Plus Drugs' biggest business and would allow medicines to be manufactured closer to where they are needed in the event of a disaster, because they're portable. One holdup, Cuban said, has been getting regulators from the US Food and Drug Administration to sign off on the pods. "We're talking to the FDA to try to get approval," he said without outlining the complications. "They're working hard to try to figure it out." Cuban campaigned for Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris in 2024 and has supported Democratic candidate James Talarico for US Senate this year in Texas. He said two items he believes the US government should immediately put in place to help lower healthcare costs would be that all payments made out of pocket should count towards patients' deductibles and that taxpayer-funded health contracts should be public without redactions. Still, Cuban said he did not believe Democrats were necessarily better than Republicans on healthcare. "None of them know what they're doing," he said.

item.title: Knicks signing Dalton Knecht to a 2-way contract
item.description: The New York Knicks are signing former first-round draft pick Dalton Knecht to a two-way deal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New York Knicks are signing former first-round draft pick Dalton Knecht to a two-way deal. The 25-year-old forward's agents with Excel Sports Management confirmed the move to ESPN on Friday. The Los Angeles Lakers selected Knecht, known in college at Tennessee as a sharpshooter, with the No. 17 overall pick of the 2024 NBA Draft. He fell out of the rotation last season and the Lakers waived him earlier this week. As a 2024-25 rookie in 78 games, Knecht averaged 9.1 points and 2.8 rebounds over 19.2 minutes per game, shooting 37.6% from 3-point range. Last season, his productivity (4.2 points, 1.4 rebounds) and minutes (10.2) were cut by about half. The Knicks will waive forward Kevin McCullar Jr., who currently occupies a two-way spot, to make room for Knecht, multiple outlets reported Friday. --Field Level Media

item.title: NFL closes Paris pop-up shop ahead of planned protests
item.description: The NFL will close its Paris pop-up shop on Saturday because of planned demonstrations in the French capital ahead of this weekend's regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, the league said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NFL will close its Paris pop-up shop on Saturday because of planned demonstrations in the French capital ahead of [USN:L1N4690K8 TEXT:"this weekend's regular-season game"] between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, the league said on Friday. The store on Rue Saint-Merri had been operating as part of events surrounding Sunday's game at the Stade de France, the first NFL regular-season contest to be held in France. "The NFL Shop on Rue Saint-Merri will be closed tomorrow Saturday 24 October, due to potential accessibility issues," the league said in a statement. The street is located in Paris' fourth arrondissement, in the city centre. The league said the shop would remain open until 8 p.m. local time on Friday and that an alternative NFL pop-up store would operate at the Stade de France on Saturday. The Steelers had already cancelled a fan event scheduled for the weekend at a bar on Place de la Bastille amid concerns over the demonstrations. France experienced some of its worst urban unrest in recent years last weekend, prompting President Emmanuel Macron's government to tighten restrictions on protests as authorities prepared for the possibility of further violence on Saturday. Sunday's game will take place in Saint-Denis, about 10 km north of Paris centre, with organisers continuing preparations despite disruption elsewhere in the city. Concerns over renewed unrest have also led several major cultural venues, including the Louvre, to close on Saturday, while the Art Basel Paris fair will remain shut throughout the weekend.

item.title: Paris looting image misidentifies woman as store owner
item.description: A video of a woman confronting masked individuals at a Paris grocery shop entrance has been mischaracterised online with unfounded details of it showing a pro-asylum activist trying to stop her boutique from being looted by the refugees she supports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A video of a woman confronting masked individuals at a Paris grocery shop entrance has been mischaracterised online with unfounded details of it showing a pro-asylum activist trying to stop her boutique from being looted by the refugees she supports. The posts , from mid-October, shared an image of a woman in a doorway with her arms outstretched, with people wearing face coverings nearby. The posts don't refer to the woman by name, though they claim she's a member of a French left-wing party and is famous for her activism in "defending North African refugees". “She owns a small chic boutique in an upscale spot, she stood in her shop trying to save it from looting and theft,” the posts said. They added that the looters "spat on her, knocked her down, and trampled her with their feet", despite the woman identifying herself and saying she was the "activist for asylum" who supported their entries and stays in France. Reuters has not identified the woman or the people wearing face coverings. However, the image is a cropped and edited screenshot from a video that contradicts parts of the posts, such as showing the woman in front of a consortium-owned convenience store chain rather than a boutique. The screenshot, which has been edited to remove graffiti from the storefront, was taken from an Instagram video posted by Paris-based photojournalist Frederic Munsch. The video shows the woman stepping into the doorway of a Franprix shop in Paris and shouting "Stop!", “Why are you doing this?” and “That’s not what the cause is about!” as masked individuals push past her into the store. Masked individuals can also be seen exiting the shop with handfuls of goods, while later shots show a smashed window and ransacked aisles inside. The woman does not introduce herself by name or mention asylum activism. She is pulled aside in the video by another person wearing a face covering and, seconds later, appears to step away. The video does not show the woman being knocked down and trampled. Franprix is a convenience store chain and part of French supermarket group Plesio , formerly Casino, owned by Czech billionaire [USN:S8N3RE0BD TEXT:"Daniel Kretinsky"]. There are more than a thousand Franprix stores in France, according to the Plesio website . Plesio’s communications department told Reuters in an email that the store in the video, situated on Rue du Faubourg du Temple, is company-owned and operated, and that the woman is not an employee. Munsch told Reuters via email that he filmed the video on October 17 at approximately 5:30 p.m. local time. He said he did not personally know the woman, though he said he believed she had been "passing by". Cost-of-living [USN:S8N42Q0F9 TEXT:"protests"] that day at the nearby Place de la Republique and in other French cities deteriorated into rioting and looting and later turned into some of the country's worst urban unrest in years. VERDICT Misleading. The video from which the image was taken shows the woman standing in the doorway of a Franprix convenience store branch, not a boutique, and the store's owners said the woman is not an employee. The posts offer no evidence for their claims about the woman's identity or the things they cite her as saying. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Chili's workers' lawsuit looks to strike New York state's lower wage for tipped workers
item.description: A lawsuit filed on Friday involving the pay practices of Chili's operator Brinker International is seeking to strike down New York state's lower minimum wage for workers who earn tips, which it claims fuels the sexual and racial harassment of workers.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: A lawsuit filed on Friday involving the pay practices of Chili's operator Brinker International (EAT.N) is seeking to strike down New York state's lower minimum wage for workers who earn tips, which it claims fuels the sexual and racial harassment of workers. The proposed class action in federal court in Brooklyn by three former Chili's employees claims that New York's policy, which most other US states share, allows Brinker to force employees to rely on tips and exposes them to unlawful discrimination. "Brinker promotes a culture in which tipped service employees make customers 'feel special,' even at the expense of their dignity and safety," the lawsuit says. Brinker did not respond to a request for comment. The New York Attorney General's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the challenge to the state law. Many worker advocates have for years called for the [USN:L1N3MD0Y5 TEXT:"elimination of sub-minimum wages"] that companies may pay to workers who earn tips under federal and most state laws, as long as tips make up the difference. In New York, where the minimum wage is $16 an hour or $17 in and around New York City, food service workers who earn tips may be paid $10.70 or $11.35 an hour. The federal tipped minimum wage is $2.13 an hour, compared with the traditional minimum wage of $7.25, and applies in states that do not set their own minimums. RELYING ON TIPS Advocates say that because tips are discretionary and unpredictable, they should supplement workers' incomes rather than make up most of their pay. The lawsuit against Brinker says that relying on tips forces workers to tolerate conduct such as sexual harassment and customers' potential racial bias. The plaintiffs' lawyers said in the lawsuit that they plan to expand the case to include a nationwide class of Chili's workers. Brinker operates more than 1,200 Chili's restaurants in the US, including 36 in New York. The company also owns Maggiano's Little Italy, an Italian restaurant chain with about 50 US locations. The lawsuit claims that Chili's reliance on customer ratings to determine workers' schedules, shifts and table assignments is also unlawful. The ratings system can be racially biased, the lawsuit says, and can make it difficult for servers to reject unwanted advances from customers for fear of a poor rating. The named plaintiffs, three former employees at a Chili's in the Glendale section of Queens in New York City, claim they were routinely subjected to sexual advances and inappropriate comments and that management did not adequately protect workers from harassment.

item.title: Senator says planned Meta commercial terms update could harm US businesses
item.description: US Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, on Friday raised concerns about Facebook parent Meta Platforms' plan to update its commercial terms, saying it could harm businesses and creators.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: US Senator Marsha Blackburn, a Tennessee Republican, on Friday raised concerns about Facebook parent Meta Platforms' (META.O) plan to update its commercial terms, saying it could harm businesses and creators. Blackburn, who is chair of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology and the Law, said the updated terms "indicate Meta is attempting to exploit American creators and businesses by granting itself sweeping authority to scrape content from any website associated with Facebook and Instagram business accounts." Earlier on Friday, Meta said it would delay the implementation of updated commercial terms from October 30 until November 20, so it can address concerns from publishers and digital advertisers. EU and UK antitrust authorities have received [USN:L6N46817D TEXT:"complaints"] about the new commercial terms, which publishers and digital advertisers said would give Meta unlimited rights to use their content for its AI services. Meta has rejected the claims. Blackburn said that Meta previously revised its terms to remove an explicit reference to AI training but said the changes did not go far enough. She added that the revised language authorizes extensive scraping of external websites and permits Meta to “develop” its business products with collected content. "Without clear restrictions on how that information may be used, including whether it may be incorporated into AI systems, Meta’s revisions offer little assurance that creators’ intellectual property will be protected," Blackburn said. She added: "This is particularly troubling for American news publishers, creators, and small businesses that rely on Meta’s platforms to reach their audiences and customers." Asked for comment on Blackburn's letter, Meta on Friday noted it had delayed the change and said the revised terms apply only to its ads and business products and that it is not changing how it uses web crawlers. "These updates don't give us new rights to supersede such preferences and this isn’t about scraping news sites," the company said, noting that "content owners will still be able to use robots.txt to signal preferences." Publishers worldwide are ramping up fights with AI companies using their content without permission to train large language models, underscoring the clash between copyright owners and those citing fair-use arguments. "Meta must withdraw the updated Commercial Terms and come to the table to protect the content of creators and publishers across the country," Blackburn said. "American creators and small businesses are not a free source of content for Meta to exploit."

item.title: Top LNG exporter QatarEnergy in talks to buy US LNG from Woodside's Louisiana plant
item.description: QatarEnergy is in talks with Woodside Energy to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas per annum (mtpa) from its Louisiana LNG plant under construction, three people with knowledge of the negotiations told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Curtis Williams, Marwa Rashad
item.content:encoded: QatarEnergy is in talks with Woodside Energy (WDS.AX) to buy up to 3 million metric tons of liquefied natural gas per annum (mtpa) from its Louisiana LNG plant under construction, three people with knowledge of the negotiations told Reuters. If a final agreement is reached, the long-term deal could see QatarEnergy buying LNG from the 16.5 mtpa export facility for between 15 and 20 years, one of the people said. Woodside Energy said on Friday it does not respond to market speculation, while QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. QatarEnergy has been buying LNG on the spot market from US exporters to supply some of its customers due to the ongoing blockage of the Strait of Hormuz as the US-Israeli war on Iran and Tehran’s strikes this year have sharply curtailed shipping. The company is also a 70% owner of the Golden Pass LNG facility being developed in Louisiana, which when complete will have the capacity to export up to 18 mtpa of LNG. On Thursday, Cheniere Energy (LNG.N) reported it had reached a long-term agreement to supply QatarEnergy with 4 mtpa of LNG. Two million metric tons per year will be sourced from Cheniere’s Sabine Pass facility in Louisiana, and another 2 mpta will come from its Corpus Christi terminal in Texas. Reuters also [USN:L1N468185 TEXT:"reported"] on Thursday that QatarEnergy is in advanced talks with Venture Global (VG.N) for a long-term supply deal to buy at least 3 million metric tons of LNG per year. Venture Global and Woodside's Louisiana LNG are the US suppliers with the most uncommitted LNG capacity. Louisiana LNG is said to be asking for a premium for liquefaction fees that exceed $2.50 per mmBtu and are above the average US market prices because of contract flexibility, offering potential buyers shorter contracts in return for higher prices, two people told Reuters.

item.title: Trump removes 50% tariffs on Canadian products to try to boost to Maine companies
item.description: President Donald Trump on Friday signed an order to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, which could boost US agriculture firms dependent on those goods.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump on Friday signed an order to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, which could boost US agriculture firms dependent on those goods. The move came after Maine Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election bid, urged the White House to address tariffs on products affecting Maine companies and farmers. Republican candidates in northern US border states most affected by the tariffs, including Maine and Michigan, are trying to strike a balance between appealing to Trump’s loyal base and winning over independent voters. Trump is exempting plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment, and packing crates and boxes, the White House said. Collins said the relief will aid the state's blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers. “These producers are a vital part of our state’s economy and support our rural and coastal communities," Collins said. "Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are ether unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense." Collins clashed with her opponent, Democrat Troy Jackson, over the subject of tariffs at an October 6 debate. Trump in August imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian imports, which took effect after talks between the two countries collapsed in August. The two have been locked in a standoff since then, though Trump on Friday asserted that Canada is working on a deal. The administration is adding certain valves, carpets, waste products, and other items to the list, the White House said. The economies of Michigan and Maine have long been intertwined with Canada’s, covering everything from auto parts to lumber to fruit-picking equipment. That has raised the stakes in two states that Republicans will likely need to win in the November 3 elections if they are to hold the US Senate.

item.title: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. wins appeal, suspension reduced to fine
item.description: Buffalo Bills safety and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr. won his appeal to overturn the one-game suspension he initially received from the NFL for allegedly spitting at an opponent.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Buffalo Bills safety and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr. won his appeal to overturn the one-game suspension he initially received from the NFL for allegedly spitting at an opponent. The league announced Friday that it reduced the punishment to a fine of $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct. Franklin will be allowed to play in Week 8 when the Bills return from their bye to face the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 1. Fellow Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was not as fortunate. His suspension for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers was upheld upon appeal on Thursday. He will be eligible to return to the active roster on Nov. 2. Per a release on Wednesday, the NFL said Franklin spat at an opposing player after Las Vegas made an extra point with 1:32 left in the fourth quarter. Franklin denied that he spat at a player and even posted a video clip to his Instagram account showing the extra-point play in slow motion. The clip cut off before the play ends. "Not a dirty play what so ever!" Franklin captioned the video clip. "Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone." His agents, Harold C. Lewis and Christian Addison, said in a statement that they "adamantly deny" Franklin spit at anyone. Franklin, 30, has recorded six tackles on special teams in six games this season. He has 124 tackles and a 99-yard interception return for a touchdown in 97 career games (nine starts) with the Carolina Panthers (2020-24) and Bills. --Field Level Media

item.title: “Íris”, de Claude Monet, torna-se obra de arte mais cara já vendida em leilão na França, diz Sotheby’s
item.description: A obra “Íris”, de Claude Monet, foi vendida na noite de quinta-feira por 50 milhões de euros (56,05 milhões de dólares), tornando-se a obra de arte mais cara já vendida em leilão na França, informou a Sotheby’s.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A obra “Íris”, de Claude Monet, foi vendida na noite de quinta-feira por 50 milhões de euros (56,05 milhões de dólares), tornando-se a obra de arte mais cara já vendida em leilão na França, informou a Sotheby’s. A pintura, concluída no final da vida de Monet, atraiu uma disputa acirrada, com seis pessoas disputando a obra por 45 minutos, antes que dois finalistas continuassem a disputa por mais 20 minutos. “Íris” acabou indo para um colecionador asiático que fez a oferta por telefone. A pintura era uma das várias obras da Coleção Schlumberger colocadas à venda no leilão e esperava-se que fosse vendida por um valor entre 22 milhões e 30 milhões de euros. O recorde anterior em leilões na França havia sido estabelecido em 2010, com a obra “Cabeça de uma Cariátide”, de Amedeo Modigliani, vendida por 43,2 milhões de euros. (Reportagem de Makini Brice)

item.title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin out Sunday with shin injury
item.description: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday's game at Detroit with a shin injury sustained in Thursday's practice.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday's game at Detroit with a shin injury sustained in Thursday's practice. "Unfortunately, Zaire, there was a little collision -- he got kneed in the shin," head coach Matt LaFleur said Friday. "So, he's going to be out this game." Franklin, 30, ranks second on the Packers (4-2) with 41 tackles through his first six starts with the team. "I don't think it's going to be anything too long-term," LaFleur added. "But, yeah, just (an) unfortunate deal. That happens when you play football, especially the way our guys have been practicing." Acquired in a March trade with Indianapolis, Franklin played his first eight NFL seasons with the Colts and made the Pro Bowl in 2024. The 2018 seventh-round draft pick has 779 tackles, 10 sacks, 11 forced fumbles and three interceptions in 138 career games (88 starts). Franklin's absence means more playing time for Ty'Ron Hopper and Isaiah McDuffie against the NFC North rival Lions (3-2). "I think we've got a lot of confidence in McDuffie, and Hopper, and Nick Niemann if need be, to go in there and do a great job for us," LaFleur said. --Field Level Media

item.title: França investiga suposto tiroteio islamofóbico contra menina perto de Paris como ato de terrorismo
item.description: Um atirador, que as autoridades suspeitam ter sido motivado por ódio islamofóbico, abriu fogo de um carro nesta sexta-feira, a oeste de Paris, matando uma pessoa e ferindo outras quatro, incluindo uma menina de 12 anos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Um atirador, que as autoridades suspeitam ter sido motivado por ódio islamofóbico, abriu fogo de um carro nesta sexta-feira, a oeste de Paris, matando uma pessoa e ferindo outras quatro, incluindo uma menina de 12 anos. “As investigações estão em andamento, mas trata-se claramente de um crime terrorista. É um ato extremamente grave”, disse o ministro do Interior, Laurent Nuñez, a repórteres no distrito de Yvelines, a oeste de Paris, onde ocorreu o ataque. Autoridades informaram que o suspeito de 39 anos, cujo nome não foi divulgado, dirigiu pela cidade de Trappes, onde disparou uma arma automática contra um posto de gasolina, um centro médico e um parque infantil. A emissora BFM informou que a menina ferida foi atingida oito vezes e estava em estado grave. “(Foi) objetivamente um ataque racista, provavelmente islamofóbico”, disse Ali Rabeh, prefeito de Trappes, cujos pais são originários de Marrocos. “As pessoas atacadas hoje poderiam muito bem ter sido minha mãe, meus irmãos ou minhas cunhadas.” A polícia conseguiu prender o homem antes que ele pudesse ferir mais alguém. Imagens de vídeo mostraram seu carro crivado de balas. O tiroteio ocorre em um momento de tensão especial na França, depois que protestos em todo o país se tornaram violentos no último sábado e antes de novas manifestações previstas para o fim de semana. Alguns políticos de extrema direita atribuíram à imigração a onda de saques e vandalismo que assolou várias cidades francesas em 17 de outubro. Rabeh, que é um político de esquerda, pediu uma condenação coletiva da retórica que “arma ideologicamente aqueles capazes de cometer tais atos”. A Promotoria Antiterrorismo, conhecida como PNAT, informou que sua investigação inclui a análise de se o tiroteio teve motivação racial ou religiosa. A PNAT pode assumir qualquer investigação criminal que considere atender aos critérios de terrorismo, incluindo violência inspirada por ideias de extrema direita. As penas por terrorismo são mais severas, e as forças antiterroristas têm maiores poderes de investigação. Nicolas Dainville, prefeito da vizinha La Verrière, disse que o suspeito morava na cidade de Plaisir, também no departamento de Yvelines, e era “de aparência europeia”. Rabeh afirmou que duas das vítimas eram de origem africana e norte-africana, respectivamente, e não forneceu detalhes sobre as origens das demais vítimas. (Reportagem de Juliette Jabkhiro, Dominique Vidalon, Zhifan Liu e Sudip Kar-Gupta)

item.title: Novartis presents weaker-than-expected relapse data for multiple sclerosis drug remibrutinib
item.description: Swiss drugmaker Novartis' oral multiple sclerosis (MS) drug remibrutinib meaningfully reduced relapses in patients, according to data presented at a medical conference in Toronto on Friday, but less than analysts had expected.
item.dc:creator: Bhanvi Satija, Marleen Kaesebier
item.content:encoded: Swiss drugmaker Novartis' (NOVN.S) oral multiple sclerosis (MS) drug remibrutinib meaningfully reduced relapses in patients, according to data presented at a medical conference in Toronto on Friday, but less than analysts had expected. The drug reduced annualized relapse rates by 35.2% and 31.2%, compared with teriflunomide, an older MS treatment sold by Sanofi under the brand name Aubagio. Analysts had expected a reduction of 45% to 60%. The detailed trial results, previously disclosed only in top-line form, were presented days after Roche (ROPC.S) released its own data on [USN:L6N4660XX TEXT:"rival MS drug"] fenebrutinib. In pooled Phase III data, Roche reported a 55% reduction in annualized relapse rate versus teriflunomide. "All in all, they might be quite similar in what they do in terms of reducing relapses and disability," Heinz Wiendl, co-chair of the Novartis studies, said in an interview. Ahead of the readout, analysts said that relapse improvements similar to those seen in Roche's trial would be needed to show that this class of treatments is better than the currently used anti-CD20 therapies. These include Ocrevus, Novartis' Kesimpta and TG Therapeutics' (TGTX.O) Briumvi, which target and kill the immune cells that drive MS. Novartis is banking on the success of the drug across different therapeutic areas, especially following a string of [USN:L4N4510T5 TEXT:"recent trial setbacks"] for its heart drug pelacarsen and muscle weakness therapy del-desiran. Analysts currently estimate remibrutinib could bring in over $4 billion in peak sales, if approved for patients with relapsing forms of MS. The two competing MS drugs belong to a class of treatments previously linked to liver toxicity, making safety a closely watched concern. While Roche's fenebrutinib could have an edge in terms of efficacy, it showed significantly higher liver enzyme elevations versus the comparator drug. Novartis said there was no liver safety signal in its drug.

item.title: Hugo Boss set to become Frasers subsidiary as stake crosses 50%
item.description: Fashion group Hugo Boss will become a subsidiary of Mike Ashley-controlled Frasers after the British retailer on Friday raised its stake in the German company to more than 50%.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Fashion group Hugo Boss (BOSSn.DE) will become a subsidiary of Mike Ashley-controlled Frasers (FRAS.L) after the British retailer on Friday raised its stake in the German company to more than 50%. Frasers, which made a [USN:L6N43B0GF TEXT:"failed €2 billion takeover bid"] for the German fashion house in June, said it had bought a further 198,666 Hugo Boss shares for about €7.6 million ($8.51 million), taking its total stake to about 34.5 million shares, or 50.08%. Hugo Boss' earnings, assets and liabilities are expected to be consolidated into Frasers' accounts as the stake passed 50%, the British firm said. A Hugo Boss spokesperson said the company had taken note of Frasers' latest stake increase, but said that crossing the 50% threshold would not have any major implications. Frasers, which has been pushing in to the premium and luxury space and ramping up its pursuit of the underperforming German designer known for its boxy men's suits, said crossing the 50% stake threshold was in the best interests of its investors. Since Hugo Boss rejected a [USN:L6N43B0GF TEXT:"€38-per-share cash offer"] as "financially inadequate," the company's chairman has stepped down and Frasers CEO Michael Murray has become the chairman of its supervisory board while the British company has steadily raised its stake. The stake purchase was funded from existing cash resources, Frasers said. Frasers shares closed 0.3% higher on Friday, while Hugo Boss ended 0.8% lower. ($1 = 0.8935 euro)

item.title: Bears TE Cole Kmet (knee) to miss rest of season
item.description: Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet is going on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chicago Bears tight end Cole Kmet is going on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed on Friday. Kmet was carted off the field in the fourth quarter of Thursday night's 30-24 home victory against the New England Patriots. He grabbed his right knee after being tackled low following an 8-yard catch and finished with three receptions for 28 yards. "He's a big part of our heartbeat," Johnson said. "It stinks. I hate it." Kmet, 27, had 10 receptions for 87 yards and one touchdown in seven games (three starts) this season. He has one season left on a four-year, $50 million contract extension signed in July 2023. Drafted by Chicago in the second round out of Notre Dame in 2020, Kmet has collected 298 catches for 3,026 yards and 22 TDs in 107 career games (94 starts). Johnson said Kmet's absence is an opportunity for 2026 third-round pick Sam Roush to step up. Roush, 23, has three catches for 33 yards in seven games this season for the Bears (5-2). "We'll be able to see the player that we drafted," Johnson said. "We had high hopes when we took him. ... I'm confident in what he's going to be able to do for us back half of the season." --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say
item.description: Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target [USN:L6N41B0XO TEXT:"undersea communications cables"] in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters. Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington collapses. The two Iranian security officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, gave few details and did not say how or where exactly Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections. "If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines ... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one of the officials said. The official warned Washington not to "play with fire", and said Iran had full access to the undersea cables and could easily destroy them. Yadollah Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure came under attack. Undersea cables carry around 99% of global internet traffic, according to the International Telecommunication Union, a UN agency. But the global impact of such attacks by Iran could be limited as less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, said Alan Mauldin, research director at telecommunications research firm TeleGeography. The strait separates Iran and Oman, linking the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. The US Department of State and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment on the Iranian security officials' remarks. There was no immediate comment from Gulf states. 'STRONGER RESPONSE' The plans for possible attacks on undersea cables reflect a conviction in Iran's leadership that a renewed US military campaign would have to be met with [USN:L8N45M1N4 TEXT:"a stronger response"] than before. Top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned this month that US-linked digital infrastructure across the Gulf, including data centres and AI facilities, could be targeted in a renewed conflict. Washington's Gulf allies have invested heavily in such infrastructure and they "should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables," the second Iranian security official said. Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran program at the Middle East Institute in Washington, said such threats were intended to deter renewed conflict and put pressure on Washington by making Gulf governments and US companies fear for their investments in the region. "Tehran wants Gulf states and corporate executives to press (US President Donald) Trump over the risks his policies pose to their investment plans," said Vatanka. Multiple cable cuts could slow internet services and disrupt financial transactions, e-commerce and cloud computing, analysts said. The impact would depend on how operators rerouted traffic and the capacity available on alternative connections, Mauldin said. Restoring connections during wartime could be difficult, experts said, and higher insurance costs and delays in obtaining permits to enter territorial waters could further complicate repairs. The Red Sea could offer a more significant target than the Strait of Hormuz, particularly if Iran had support from its Houthi allies in Yemen, though Tehran has made no public statement indicating it plans to target cables there. The Red Sea carries data between Europe, East Africa and Asia, with capacity routed through it accounting for about 3% of global international demand and around 10% of traffic travelling between regions, Mauldin said. Gulf governments have been investing heavily in technology to diversify beyond oil and become global artificial intelligence hubs, deepening ties with US technology firms. Iranian strikes directly hit two Amazon Web Services facilities in the UAE in March and damaged infrastructure near one of its facilities in Bahrain. The IRGC named US tech companies including Microsoft, Google, Apple and Nvidia as legitimate targets at the height of the war in March. Land-based connections can provide alternative routes for internet traffic, and Gulf states and US technology companies are investing in additional infrastructure to improve resilience. [USN:S8N43F050 TEXT:"Microsoft plans to invest"] more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030.

item.title: Trump and Burnham discuss North Sea oil, Ukraine and Falklands
item.description: US President Donald Trump said he discussed opening up North Sea oil during a conversation with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, as well as touching on the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine "very lightly."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said he discussed opening up North Sea oil during a conversation with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, as well as touching on the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine "very lightly." "They're opening up the North Sea oil," Trump told reporters at the White House before departing for a campaign trip to Florida ahead of the November 3 midterm US elections. "I've been after them to do that for two years... Andy is getting it done." On Wednesday, Trump praised Britain's approval of the [USN:L8N46707X TEXT:"Jackdaw North Sea gas field"], a decision that ended years of legal and political wrangling, though British officials said a decision about the bigger Rosebank oilfield was yet to be made. Burnham's office said in a statement that the two leaders agreed the Jackdaw approval would bring "significant benefits" to Britain. They also welcomed continued cooperation between British and US companies, particularly on nuclear power. Burnham also raised the topic of oil exploration off the [USN:L6N45F0WA TEXT:"Falkland Islands,"] a largely self-governing British overseas territory whose sovereignty Argentina has long disputed. Burnham spoke about the economic consequences for Britain and the US of what he described as Argentina's coercive [USN:S0N44M029 TEXT:"measures"] seeking to halt the drilling and reiterated the importance of respecting the islanders' right to develop their natural resources, Downing Street added. On Ukraine, Burnham underlined the importance of Kyiv having full access to [USN:L6N4690ZQ TEXT:"Starlink"] to defend itself against Russia and welcomed Trump's efforts to bring Russian President Vladimir Putin to the negotiating table. The leaders agreed to work with international partners to end the bloodshed, the statement said. The leaders also discussed the Middle East, with Burnham reaffirming Britain's support for Saudi Arabia in the face of [USN:L1N46809Q TEXT:"Houthi attacks"].

item.title: Rendimientos EEUU suben ligeramente, título a 10 años sigue por debajo 5% ante nerviosismo por IA
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el viernes, un día después de que el rendimiento de referencia a 10 años registrara su mayor caída diaria en casi cuatro años, aunque se mantenían bajo el umbral del 5% debido a la persistente preocupación por la sostenibilidad del repunte de las acciones relacionadas con la IA.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron el viernes, un día después de que el rendimiento de referencia a 10 años registrara su mayor caída diaria en casi cuatro años, aunque se mantenían bajo el umbral del 5% debido a la persistente preocupación por la sostenibilidad del repunte de las acciones relacionadas con la IA. *El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años de referencia subió 3,7 puntos básicos, hasta el 4,99%. El rendimiento a 10 años ha bajado unos 11 puntos básicos en la semana y va camino de registrar su tercera semana consecutiva de descensos, su racha bajista más larga desde junio. *Los inversionistas se han decantado por activos más seguros, como la deuda pública, ante las recientes preocupaciones sobre la sostenibilidad de la tendencia alcista de la IA, un componente clave del actual mercado de la renta variable. El reciente repunte del mercado de bonos se ha producido a pesar de que los datos económicos apuntan a presiones continuadas sobre los precios y de que el petróleo ha superado los 100 dólares por barril. *Sin embargo, mientras que el sector tecnológico del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) subió a medida que se disipaban los temores sobre la IA, el índice S&P 500 en su conjunto (.SPX) retrocedió. *El rendimiento de los bonos a 10 años se desplomó 19,3 puntos básicos el jueves, su mayor caída desde el 10 de marzo de 2023, cuando las autoridades reguladoras cerraron SVB Financial Group tras el fallido intento del banco de obtener capital. *"Volveremos a ver rendimientos superiores al 5% para el bono a 10 años. No estamos tan lejos, pero tampoco es como para decir: “Oh, vale, ya estamos en plena carrera”", afirmó JoAnne Bianco, socia y estratega senior de inversiones de BondBloxx Investment Management en Chicago. *"Sigue habiendo muchos factores adversos, como la inflación persistente, la creciente oferta de bonos del Tesoro para financiar los déficits, la necesidad general —con toda la incertidumbre que ello conlleva— de primas de plazo más elevadas y, además, los precios más altos de la energía, que parecen que van a mantenerse durante un tiempo". *El rendimiento del bono a 30 años subió 2,9 puntos básicos hasta el 5,316%, pero bajó casi 13 puntos básicos en la semana, encaminándose además hacia su tercera semana consecutiva de descensos. *A pesar de que los datos económicos apuntan a un aumento de las presiones sobre los precios, las expectativas del mercado respecto a una subida de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal en su reunión de política monetaria de la próxima semana se han desvanecido. La probabilidad de una subida de al menos 25 puntos básicos se ha reducido al 9,4%, según el CME FedWatch, desde el 15,5% de hace una semana y el 70,9% de hace un mes. *Un indicador muy seguido de la curva de rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, que mide la diferencia entre los rendimientos de los bonos a 2 y a 10 años —y que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas—, se situó en 29,6 puntos básicos positivos. *El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a dos años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, subió 5,5 puntos básicos hasta el 4,69%, lo que supone un descenso de unos 5 puntos básicos en la semana, lo que representaría la cuarta semana consecutiva de caídas, su racha más larga del año. *La tasa de equilibrio de los Títulos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos protegidos contra la inflación (TIPS) a 5 años se situó por última vez en el 2,456%, en camino de alcanzar su cierre más alto desde el 10 de septiembre, tras cerrar el jueves en el 2,38%. *La tasa de equilibrio de los TIPS a 10 años se situaba en el 2,346%, lo que indica que el mercado prevé una inflación media de alrededor del 2,3% anual durante la próxima década.

item.title: Zelenskiy says Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators to meet in early November in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of the countries' leaders would follow.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of the countries' leaders would follow. Zelenskiy said he spoke with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Friday after their meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier this week. He said any peace agreement would need strong security guarantees for Ukraine and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army. "The plan is to meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course," Zelenskiy told the Hudson Institute think tank via a video link. He said much would depend on Russia, noting that a similar meeting expected this month had not materialized. Zelenskiy stressed the importance of continued diplomatic efforts to reach a ceasefire and end the war, now in its fifth year, adding that Europe should also be involved in the talks. The Ukrainian president said it was critical for the technical discussions to be followed by a meeting of the countries' leaders. He said he hoped to have another meeting with the US negotiators, adding that Ukraine was ready to start negotiating on a full ceasefire, or even an agreement covering just the energy sector, or maritime operations, if Moscow was unwilling to discuss a broader deal. He also welcomed the return of 270 soldiers who had been captive in Russia, but said further exchanges were needed, with some Ukrainian troops held in Russia for over 12 years since Russia's annexation of the Crimea region. "If they want to raise any topic, we are ready, but territories is a sensitive issue which can be (addressed) during discussions on the level of leaders," he said. The White House had no immediate comment on the plans for a trilateral meeting at the technical level. Ukraine's military was still grappling with access to Starlink communications systems, which Ukraine uses for battlefield communications and drone operations, Zelenskiy said, despite US assurances that speed restrictions had been removed. "The speed limits on Starlink and Starshield are still there, and the speed has not been restored," he said, contradicting a statement by US President Donald Trump that the services had been fully restored. Zelenskiy said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had assured him in a phone call that the satellite communications services would be restored within 48 to 72 hours, but that had not occurred, degrading Kyiv's ability to defend against Russian attacks. "On the civilian sector and also closer to the frontline, we still have the same limit, 161 kilometers per hour maximum, so it means 100 miles," he said. The limits make it impossible for Ukraine to counter Russia's jet-powered drones, which travel at speeds of around 280 miles per hour, officials have said. Ukraine was also waiting for a shipment of air defense interceptors that had been previously agreed, Zelenskiy said, complicating Ukrainian defensive efforts in the face of nearly daily massive attacks by Russian drones and missiles. He expressed frustration about Western moves to relax some sanctions against Russia that he said were enabling Moscow to continue its war against Ukraine. "Sanctions work, but total sanctions," he said. "If you put, please put, don't lift." Trump this month announced an agreement for Russia to supply diesel to the United States for the first time since 2022, and temporarily waived parts of a new US sanctions law against Russia.
